title: Marginal moments of a GLMM
html:
In @def-gmm-glmm write μi(u)=h(ηi) and μiM=E{μi(u)}.

  1. E(Yi)=μiM, Var(Yi)=ϕwiE[V{μi(u)}]+Var{μi(u)},{#eq-gmm-marginal-variance}

    and Cov(Yi,Yk)=Cov{μi(u),μk(u)} for i≠k. The marginal variance always exceeds the average conditional variance.

  2. Binomial. If Yi∣u∼Bin{Ni,πi(u)} and π¯i=Eπi(u), then E(Yi)=Niπ¯i and Var(Yi)=Niπ¯i(1−π¯i){1+(Ni−1)Var{πi(u)}π¯i(1−π¯i)}.{#eq-gmm-binomial-overdispersion}

    The overdispersion factor is the beta-binomial one, and it equals 1 when Ni=1: a single Bernoulli response carries no trace of the random effect.

  3. Poisson with a log link, ϕ=1, and a random intercept ui∼N(0,τ2) shared by the observations of a cluster. Then 𝛃μijM=exp⁡(x(ij)⊤β+τ2/2), Var(Yij)=μijM+(μijM)2(eτ2−1),Cov(Yij,Yik)=μijMμikM(eτ2−1).{#eq-gmm-poisson-moments}

    The marginal variance function is exactly the NB2 function V(μ)=μ+μ2/κ of @def-cnt-negbin, with κ=1/(eτ2−1) — although the marginal distribution is not negative binomial and has no closed form.
